data: Masterpiece of a game amazing story and super fun
Great game, very good story and gameplay plus repay value is pretty good too, definitely recommend it for anyone looking for old
The game is incredible: beautiful atmosphere, amazing story, fun gameplay, fantastic soundtrack, and plenty of extras
easy to run, fun, great story, 11/10 soundtrack
Its a pretty good game and if you are into games like half-life and other FPS's I would definitely recommend it
The gala of bugs and crashes is just not worth it
the gameplay is repetitive and not fun
my game crashes each time i even do anything and it never crashed not even in the story mode
The game stutters constantly, making fights tedious and hacking annoying
Would not recommend until they patch the game (
how in the remaster you dont fix the dogshit autosave, game crashes at the end of a level hours lost
Terrible "remaster" ran into so many crashes and bugs already in the first hour
Played for 5 hours only for the game to non stop crash and corrupt the save files for no apparent reason
the gameplay and movement feel so slow and I hate the hacking puzzles and refused to even attempt them
It's mostly in the lack of movement options, compounded by the fact that every enemy has the most insane auto-aim you've ever seen
It pops up constantly, disrupts the pacing of combat, and gets repetitive pretty fast
the ending portion of the game was pretty underwhelming
Unfortunately, once the central twist is revealed, the narrative loses much of its momentum
I just feel like I wanted to focus more on the story,
(its not cheating if i got cheated first) overall, i got my play out of it
The hacking minigame is atrocious, and I believe in the next few games they attempted to make it less boring,
Hacking gets quite repetitive without mentioning how some of them are impossible to solve (alarm and broken tiles blocking every way)

This game is so much fucking fun. The story that you tag along in for this is so good, the whole concept of this underwater world is just pulls everyone in from start to finish. This game is honestly just magic. Much respect goes to 2K, this is one of the best games I'll ever play and get ahold of.

Amazing story and fun gameplay, plasmids were such a cool mechanic for its time and the big daddies still give me nightmares. the designs are amazing, the maps are great. Overall one of my favorite games
this is a great game and it has a great story and it is a classic game the entire series is great i would recommend all of them

Bioshock masterfully weaves together narrative and gameplay elements in a way rarely seen at all in other games. By far my favorite level was Fort Frolic, because it uses worldbuilding and visual elements to show, and not tell, the history of Rapture and the citizens that used to dwell within it.

I encountered absolutely no bugs or glitches throughout my playthrough, and I had no crashes at all. I'm not sure if I was just lucky, or if the game has been patched enough now that the issues are gone.
Man, this game is really great. If only it had a remaster so it could run on modern hardware without crashing every less-than-five minutes.

I bought BioShock 1.. a long time ago and I never got around to it until now, conveniently, years after it was upgraded to this version of the game.

I just finished the game now, 2 minutes after writing this review. This is.. a MUST PLAY game for everyone.

One of the best games I've ever played.

Played the full game on Steam Deck and had zero issues, it actually stunned me how well this looked here. When docked, I had a few controller disconnect issues when inactive for short time however a simple controller reorder in the Decks settings helped that. Had no save issues or audio problems aswell as graphics looking incredible too, a totally normal run-through experience which allowed me to 100% finish the game (achievements, challenge maps and all)

The game itself is just a masterpiece of the genre and if you have never played BIOSHOCK before I would absolutely recommend checking it out. The story, atmosphere and progression are great and it is such a gem.

BioShock is an absolute masterpiece. The gripping story, solid gameplay, and thematic implementation of its challenging of human free will combine to form an experience that would require the divine intervention to forget. As long as you know where you're going, the game doesn't drag anywhere. Buy and play through the entirety of this game, it's absolutely worth your money and time.

If you like Half-Life/Black Mesa/Bendy and the Ink Machine, you will like this.

Great, fun game, runs like a dream with good graphics on my potato of a PC.

Would 100% recommend!

this game was a lot of fun that had been carried by the villain and the big daddy's (robot guy on the cover)

this game is really like a cross between half life 2 and bendy and the ink machine, smooth gunplay with fun abilities and a great way to give the player a decision, and maybe one of the greatest plottwists in gaming

my only problem with the game is the uselesness of some of the plasmids (gadgets). and the game feels a bit too long for some reason

unexpected fun, ''a man chooses, a slave obeys'' still gives me chills 7.6/10

Just finished the game, and thoroughly enjoyed it. I'd originally only played Infinite, so I have no point of reference between the original and remastered version.

But to sum it up, there was a point (that point!) and it gave me chills. I will play it again, and it will continue to give me chills. I would recommend this to anyone who is done with generic FPSs. It's clever, its entertaining, and it will certainly make you think.

Overall a great game from the satisfying combat combining abilities and guns making combat fun and fresh with varieties of ways to kill the inbred splicers, an atmosphere that does a great job at immersing you into the visually orgasmic underwater city of Rapture sometimes making you unsettled and other times making you just admire the world of Rapture and then the story, arguably one of the best stories ever written in a video game packed with moments that will frighten you, moments that will make you emotional moments that will shock you with a broad range of great, memorable characters although the game does slightly decrease in quality towards the last few hours (mostly in the combat as only a few weapons are really viable and the final boss isn't very good at all) I'd still highly recommend that if you haven't already, would you kindly just play this brilliant game.

I am so late to playing this game, but it was worth every minute! Excellent sound design, art style, story, gameplay/weapons, all a blast. I found myself constantly exploring the environment because you never know what you’ll find.

Great atmosphere, story and general idea.

Can get boring and easy at times. I played it on hard without any difficulty throughout the game. In my opinion, the last hour is pretty bad .

A great game from the X360/PS3 era, with a fun set of weapons, a unique locale, and interesting characters. Shitty morale choice does poke its ugly head though. Just do the good choice unless you deliberately want to be a bastard. Only reason to choose the evil path is to get a few more upgrade points for killing them, but choosing the good path gives almost the same number of points and a few special abilities you can't get otherwise.

Fantastic game, however you cant ignore the bugs that are found. For the develepors knowledge about 60% of the time I enter/leave the gene swap interface, the game will crash. Just make sure you save a lot!

Apparently this was the oldest game I owned that I had not played... prolly because of how long I have owned the original Bioshock.

I do feel that this review is somewhat redundant since i've already reviewed Bioshock, deleted that, reviewed it again, and am now set to reviewing it a third time. I hope you will forgive me if I don't really feel up to saying much about this. Well, I guess it is "remastered" and looks prettier and all that. But at its core, this is still Bioshock more or less how it was originally.

If it seems like I am forgetting some major changes that may or may not have been added to this remaster, then it is probably because it has been so long since I played the original, and I wasn't terribly into it back then. Or at least not crazy into it.

Anyway, it's Bioshock 1 again, but with some little technical updates so it looks nicer and all that. As a game, it's fine. Probably pretty good, actually. If you haven't played this already, then you may as well check this out! :D

A good game.
Doesn't overstay its welcome.
I've finished it in nearly 12 hours on the lowest difficulty, but expect to spend a couple more hours on higher difficulties.
I really really enjoyed Bioshock, the story and world building was phenomenal, combat was fun, and I always felt immersed

I was very late to Bioshock, but fell in love with it immediately. The setting and the story are unlike any other, and it's become my top 3 game universes of all time. It's truly a very unique and special experience, complete with action, tension, and incredible world building.

Don't underestimate this game or it's ability to scare the living shit out of you!
And now you can be scared with HD graphics!

The atmosphere on this game is petrifying and alarming, it's a soul chilling experience and it's still unmatched on the Bioshock series on it's ability to make you feel uneasy and unsafe.

Totally recommend this.

I don't care what type of gamer or person you are, I believe Bio shock to be a must own. This game is excellent, easily has some of the best storytelling in any video game. For it being a game of the past (2007) it still stands out as one I'll continue returning too, due to it's exciting atmosphere of mysterious, eerie, and very capturing with plenty of action and varied game play. It's in my top 10 of all time, and that's saying something.
Decent story with a good amount of mystery to it, the atmosphere and the environment of Rapture is so well done

I'll take any excuse to play BioShock again. That coupled with the fact that I got this game free of charge because I already owned the original BioShock means I can't really complain despite the minor setback I encountered when I first tried to play. The game has some problems on computers using AMD hardware apparently. I don't know exactly what but that seems to be a problem a lot of people, myself included, ran into. Fortunately for me I upgraded to an Nvidia graphics card shortly after and the problem didn't resurface. This isn't really a "solution" though but it isn't my problem anymore so it doesn't bother me too much, heh.

It's just a remastered edition so there isn't really anything to say.

TL;DR; It doesn't crash anymore, but there are still some minor bugs and glitches. Overall its playable now.

Now I love this game so much its literally my username. So I was pissed when I initially saw the state the remaster was in. I decided to come back to it now after a few years to try and get some free achievements and I can tell you they definitely improved the build. Way back when I literally couldn't get the game to launch without crashing. Now I beat the game with no crashing and only a few bugs to speak of. First, the AI sometimes does some weird ballerina shit and gets stuck on stairs or pillars. Second, sometimes lighting effects such as electrical sparks will cause weird flashing boxes to appear on screen (serious epilepsy warning). Third, the sound engine is completely fucked. You'll hear enemies that are on different floors, in different rooms, behind three doors and a fire like they are standing right next to you. As for frame rate I get a solid 120 no problem, usually higher with very infrequent dips into the 60s when the game gets really busy. Overall it is night and day from when it first released and I can recommend giving it a try assuming you can overlook the few bugs I've listed.

My review to Bioshock™ Remastered

In Bioshock™ Remastered you play a person who explores and gets to the bottom of the truth about himself and his memories of his family in the undersea city of Rapture. I love the setting of the city and its different places and locations. There are also many enemy types and of course the big daddy. Also there are audio files to collect, shoot photos of different enemies and explore them through that. There are also the little sisters that you can save or exploit. I have saved them all though.:) And there are also many different tonikas and plasmids. Weapon upgrade stations as well as different weapons and weapon ammo.
Would you kindly...? Yes absolutely! ;)

Pro:
+ 65 Steam-achievements
+ Full controller support
+ Steam Deck Compatibility playable
+ Developer commentary available
+ Remote Play
+ Challenge rooms

Contra:
- Nothing for me

I definitely recommend this game!

Still holds up as easily one of my favourite games of all time, the world building and storytelling in the environment alone is masterful. Exploring Rapture and meeting its "inhabitants" is both terrifying and wildly interesting.
Do yourself a favour if you never got around to this classic, grab it and enjoy.
Great dystopian shooter. Rapture is an amazing setting, the perks are a good idea and big daddys/little sisters will haunt me in my dreams. The story was really surprising for me. Excellent game!

Now I see what all the hype is about. I wanted to try out the Bioshock series and started with the first game. Very interesting storyline and atmosphere. Lots of action and good progression to finding out what happens at the end. It makes me curious to know if an underwater city could actually function. Either way, I look forward to playing the sequel games.

The gameplay is good but the game crashes a lot and loses saves :( i was excited for the weekend and played a lot in one day, the game crashed now i have to do 2 levels again because it didnt save apparently. I like to explore everything in a level so it took me a pretty big chunk of my day to get to where i was and was happy about my progress and i didnt know if the game suddenly crashes you lose progress :( as soon as i found out that i lost so much progress and so much time was wasted i uninstalled the game right on the spot.

I heard great things about this game but i was very disappointed. I understand it's quite dated now but even when you put it against similar games of the same generation, in my opinion, it doesn't stand tall.
Story line was weak and slow. The characters are ridiculous and even the powers and weapons are dull.
I played it as it was always on my list of games to be played but i don't think I'll be continuing the series if this is what i'm in for for another two games.

Such a great game, it really requires skill to get through this game on higher difficulties. I love how you can approach every combat situation with the use of plasmids and other weapons. The story of Rapture City is also very entertaining I was hooked through out the whole game wanting to know more and why everything happened. Now on to Bioshock 2 *Whoosh*

Very amazing fps game that I have never played before . The game is awesome with amazing story line and ton of map exploration. The game graphics are good but I think original one and remastered one look similar as I see in youtube videos but anyways it doesn't matter which one you play . The game is combination of horror and action which is pretty cool and the underwater exploration is fantastic. The weapon combat style and power ability (Phasmid) are just amazing and feels more interesting to make chaos and having fun in it . The game length is kind of medium ,not too long and not too short. The best thing I like in this game is chapter length, the devs make so much fun at making chapter that they make curious to players about exploring,solving puzzles,etc. Overall this game is really good and you can try this game it is totally amazing than I expected with story rich,exploration,characters,gameplay,etc . I will give rating to this game 9.7/10

One of the greats, a few things haven't aged crazy well like the ADS but the story and environment are second to none in my opinion. If you've never tried Bioshock or just haven't played it since Xbox 360 days you definitely should pick this up!
This game was a lot of fun. Remastered made it really worth playing even for a game that is now 17 years old. Bioshock is full of action and chaos, giving a unique experience. Loved it.

As a game? It's fantastic! Gameplay is still great and the story and atmosphere are nearly unmatched even today. Upgrading weapons and seeing the model visually change is probably the most satisfying part and is something even Infinite couldn't figure out. There are some really annoying aspects that really don't make much sense even for 2006. For instance, having to switch hands between guns and plasmids is a weird choice and the last level is really bad. It's overall very good, though.

But as a program? This remaster has to be the single most unstable piece of software I've ever used. It is appalling to me that this was ever approved as a final product. This game crashed so often and so hard that I had to save every time I wanted to open the map. It would often also crash when trying to save.

It is recommended because I'm fairly certain you still get the original release when you buy the remaster. Buy it, and play that version instead. It cannot be worse than this. And even if it is, at least you have the reassurance that it's that way because of its age. Dev commentary is pretty cool. I like Geoff Keighley.

🌊 BioShock – A Beautiful Nightmare Under the Sea
🕹️ Playtime: ~15–20 hours
👍 Recommended

🧠 What It Gets Right:
🏙️ Atmosphere & Worldbuilding

Rapture, the sunken 1960s utopia-turned-dystopia, is jaw-droppingly creative

Every room tells a story: neon signs, broken glass, whispers in the walls 🧱💡

Feels like you're living in a fallen dream, not just playing a game

🎨 Art Direction & Tone

Stylized visuals walk the line between cartoonish and disturbing 😨🎭

The juxtaposition creates a unique tone you won’t find anywhere else

📚 Strong Narrative & Surprising Climax

The story ramps up beautifully, culminating in a twist that redefines everything

Minimal but effective storytelling through environmental design and audio logs 🎧

⚠️ What Holds It Back:
🔫 Repetitive Combat

Most enemies = splicers who charge you screaming. Cool at first, but gets old

Combat lacks variety; fights become predictable over time 🤷‍♂️

🗣️ Lack of Interactive Dialogue

Would benefit from player-driven conversations or choices beyond fighting

Dialogue is atmospheric, but more interactivity could’ve elevated immersion

💬 Final Thoughts:
“BioShock is a haunting descent into madness, philosophy, and power—all wrapped in one of gaming’s most memorable settings. The gameplay doesn't always live up to the brilliance of its world, but the story alone is worth the trip to Rapture.”

⭐ Score: 8.5/10
🎖️ Come for the story. Stay for the atmosphere. Tolerate the combat.

One of my most beloved classics! Very good with variety and atmosphere. Good for several playthroughs.
Remastered mostly for just compatibility. And why not. Since "all good things flow into Rapture".
game was great but got a bug where the game got stuck besides that great game plus wached a bunch of girls jab a person to death
This game gave me anxiety if I didn't save every 10 minutes because it crashes so often I would lose all of my progress. However the story made up for the lack of optimization on PC.

The first bioshock stands up to time both story and gameplay, so why not re-vamp the visuals.

Rapture looks even more stunning in 108op. The director commentary and the museum are fantastic additions. I haven't played the time trial missions yet, but will in time. After three playthroughs, the game still doesn't get old.

That being said, I have hit a few technical issues over the 20plus hours of playtime. 4 ot 5 crashes after a couple hours of grinding. Okay, its to be expected......but when I reload the game, my last save file would sometimes disappear. Bioshock can be a bit unforgiving with its autosave frequency. I've found from other reviews that you SHOULD ALWAYS MAKE A NEW SAVE/NEVER OVERWRITE A SAVE. Unless of course you like grinding through story over and over. :)

If support fixed this problem, easily 9/10.
I don't actually like it much - but this is an information review to say that the bugs described by all the other reviews seem to have since been patched as of 10/03/2021.

Just finished this again recently after haven't played it since the days of owning on the Xbox 360. Definitely not a perfect game, the moral choice of harvesting or rescuing the little sisters is made almost meaningless with rescuing being rewarded almost to the same degree as harvesting. For example I finished the game on the hardest diffuculty and was so overpowered in the later sections of the game that I could simply run around with just the wrench and electro shock plasmid saving my plentiful ammo for Big Daddy encounters. So in truth there is really no reason to go down the evil path unless of course you want to see that ending. I also think there was far too much emphasis placed on hacking, with gene tonics making it incredibly easy to hack every single turret/drone/camera/vending mahcine etc. that you encounter, meaning that it feels like a significant portion of your playtime is spent in the satisfying but repetetive hacking puzzle minigame. 

All that aside the story, worldbuilding, atmosphere, music and voice acting are all amazing and the combat is simple but fun. The kind of retro futuristic art deco aesthetic is super unique and well thought out not falling into many of the corny traps that games with a similar aesthetic fall into, I would say I think it is better than Fallout's super on the nose 1950s atomic age retro futurism, but that is of course my subjective opinion.

Kinda ashamed to admit this but i played this game for the first time in big 2026 and absolutely loved it! The remaster is really good because the gameplay doesn't feel dated at all.

Bioshock is kinda iconic so i don't really need to convince you to play this game but if you are planning on playing, play the remaster unlike Bioshock 2 remaster which is a mess.
Would you kindly… play this game? This isn’t just a game - it’s art. One of the best experiences I’ve had. I even finished it twice to fully absorb the story.
Theres a reason why this game is infinitely considered as an artwork and if you get this version, youre in for an eye popping ride with a twist that still stands strong even after all these years
this port is utter dogshit and crashed my pc yet i am still going to give it a yes because of how good this game is

Rapture is a deeply captivating world with an unforgettable twist and cool gunplay, though swapping hands between weapons and Plasmids can feel a bit tricky.

Overall: 8.5/10. A masterpiece of atmospheric storytelling.

remaster my ass, its a completely botched port. 2k farmed it out to some noname developer, who apparently had no fucks to give here. the result is a buggy mess that is borderline unplayable:

- less graphics options than an assetflip unity game in early access (the original had plenty)
- no fov options exept a toggle that increases it from eyecancer to vomitenducing
- no surround sound (the original had 7.1)
- flickering textures
- terrible mouse input (accelaration, smoothing, hypersensitivity)
- frequent crashes that reset difficulty (bye, bye achievements), key bindings and any change you might have made to the .ini files to try and fix the other issues

if this would cost money, i'd say avoid like the plague.

reason.text: Negative reviews from this period mostly object to a 2K launcher added in an update, with reviews describing it as tied to a 2K account and collecting user data.
Reviews also report broken Linux support, crashes, and an unplayable game, and an official announcement says 2K are aware of possible impacts from the recent update.
